title: Towards Realistic Models of Change: A Causal Perspective on Decision-Making and Dynamical Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.28803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While statistical learning has made remarkable progress in recent decades, driven by large datasets and data-driven protocols that have transformed scientific practice, it still faces a key limitation: it struggles to generalize beyond the data it has seen, often failing under distribution shift. Causality offers a promising solution: causal models focus on the underlying mechanisms of change rather than surface-level associations, enabling robust reasoning under external interventions. This allows systems not only to learn from data, but also to reason about hypothetical scenarios, adapt to new environments, and inform better decisions. This thesis explores how these approaches can inform each other, in two parts.   The first part examines algorithmic recourse, that is, identifying which changes an individual can make to overturn an unfavorable decision. translated_title: 迈向现实的变革模型：决策与动力系统的因果视角
translated_abstract: 尽管统计学习在近几十年中取得了显著进展——这得益于大型数据集和改变科学实践的数据驱动方法——但它仍面临一个关键局限：难以泛化到已见数据之外，在分布偏移下常常失效。因果性提供了一个有前景的解决方案：因果模型关注变化背后的底层机制而非表面关联，能够在外部干预下进行稳健推理。这使得系统不仅能从数据中学习，还能对假设情景进行推理、适应新环境并支持更好的决策。本论文分两部分探讨这些方法如何相互启发。第一部分研究算法追索权，即识别个体可以做出哪些改变以推翻不利决策，我们针对已有框架提出了一种替代视角，主张……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文从因果视角研究决策与动力系统中的现实变革模型，其第一部分针对算法追索权问题提出了有别于既有框架的新视角，旨在识别个体可采取哪些行动来推翻不利的决策。
en_tdlr: This thesis takes a causal perspective on realistic models of change in decision-making and dynamical systems, proposing an alternative to the established algorithmic recourse framework for identifying which changes individuals can make to overturn unfavorable decisions.
